data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "Two conclusions are the same claim iff they are counterfactually dependent: retracting one would necessarily force retraction of the other, and vice versa, within the system's current justification network.", "mechanism": "The system maintains a directed acyclic graph of justifications. When two conclusions C1 and C2 appear to agree, the system simulates retraction of C1 by temporarily removing its supporting justifications and propagating the removal. If C2 loses all support and must be retracted, and the symmetric test from C2 to C1 also holds, then C1 and C2 are identical claims. Otherwise they are distinct.", "scope": {"covers": ["conclusions with explicit justifications", "deterministic reasoning systems"], "excludes": ["conclusions from independent oracle sources", "probabilistic beliefs without crisp justifications"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions pass the retraction test but are intuitively different because they are logically equivalent given the axioms, yet one is about 'Socrates is mortal' and the other about 'Plato is mortal' derived from different universal statements.", "eval": "program:retraction_test_equiv_check"}], "prose_notes": "This criterion captures causal dependence rather than mere logical equivalence. It risks over-merging when the system's axioms tightly couple distinct domains."}
